name: IL-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong R lean of IL-12 (PVI R+22)
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Bost's incumbency and overwhelming financial advantage, and prediction markets pricing him near 96% all point to a safe Republican hold; the Democratic challenger has raised little and drawn no outside spending.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or unexpected outside spending surge could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican incumbent Mike Bost is seeking another term in a southern Illinois district that leans heavily Republican, with a partisan advantage of about 22 points. Bost has raised more than $1.3 million and holds roughly $790,000 on hand, while Democratic challenger Julie Fortier has raised under $90,000 with no outside support on either side. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Bost about a 96% chance of winning.

The fundamentals point firmly toward a Republican hold. The district's lean, Bost's incumbency, and his financial edge all align, and the favorable national environment for Republicans adds further cushion. Fortier would need an extraordinary shift to compete; the realistic range of outcomes runs from a comfortable Bost win to a landslide.
